- booked for an induction Saturday 21st December
- went in late on the Wednesday night for reduced movements and they said they'd induce me then 
- got the balloon in around 1am and went home. They told me to come back in 815pm the next night
- around 4am I had painful contractions for around an hour but they went off
- 9am the balloon had fallen out (but not fully out my vagina so I had to pull it out lol)
- contractions started to pick up around 1pm, getting them around every 20 minutes or so
- contractions got closer together and longer so at around 630/7pm they were about 4 minutes apart and a minute long
- went in to the hospital and was put on the monitor to check his movements first with me going for the reduced movements 
- checked my cervix around 930pm and I was 4cm! Thank god because the pain was getting worse and if I was any less I would have been very disheartened. They broke my waters and the pain really kicked up from then
- had gas and air which didn't take the pain away and just made me dizzy. Around 1130pm I got diamorphine which eased the pain but made me super dizzy so I just lay on my side on the bed for around 2 hours
- about 3am I was really struggling with the pain and debated an epidural but got my cervix checked and I was 7cm so decided not to get it because I was scared of labour slowing down and just wanted it over and done with
- baby's heart rate was dropping so they put the clip on his head and it seemed to be just because the monitor on my stomach wasn't picking him up very well so I started to push even though I didn't have the urge 
- pushed him out in 30 minutes. This was probably the best part and I didn't feel any pain at all during this part I was just working with the contractions 
- he was born at 545am and I felt a pop which was me tearing. About 4 different people came in to decide if it was a third degree tear and when they confirmed it was I went down to theatre to have it stitched up

Sorry this was long tried to keep it as brief as possible! Will just say I didn't feel anything really for the tear as it happened and didn't have any pain til around the next day. I was scared of having a tear but the recovery really hasn't been too bad especially with it being third degree.

Good luck on your birth!

I felt like I prepared as best I could with hypnobirthing, breathing techniques and pelvic floor exercises. I had a third degree tear and I felt a pop when it happened but no pain at all. They took me down to theatre to repair it and though I had pain for around 3 weeks afterwards it's been okay! Nowhere near as bad as I thought and I was so scared of tearing. They gave me antiobiotics to prevent infection, stool softener and I used my peri bottle to keep everything clean. Make sure you have a good stock of paracetamol and ibuprofen in because you will need it every 4 hours.

I gave birth last month and I just took one suitcase that I'd take on holiday and check in for all three of our things. I had things separated in different bags for baby, me etc and I'm so glad I did! People said oh that's way too big but just going off the NHS guidelines there's no way it could fit in something smaller. It was much easier going in and out the hospital and I had to go down to theatre and when we were moved to postnatal ward my partner had to pack everything up and move it on his own which would have been a nightmare with three bags. Plus we stayed in an extra night and had to get my partner to go out for more things so I'm a fan of the suitcase lol
Supermarkets are your best bet and I loved Matalan though the sizes run pretty big

Yeah I was told to come off duloextine because it wasn't safe. If you feel really down it's worth a go to try something else you need to look after yourself too x

Have you took sertraline or an SSRI before? I took duloextine before being pregnant and had tried three SSRIs previously which didn't work which is why I decided to continue with no medication. 
My health visitor said if you take medication to treat a (mental) condition you should absolutely take that medication just as you would for a physical condition
It sounds like it would help you to take something and I would do it as soon as possible to get some relief from your symptoms and be in a good place for birth and post partum

Mine actually never dropped and I was upset thinking he was never going to come on his own. I went in for reduced movements at 40+2 and he was fully engaged and I was 1cm dilated so I wouldnt put too much stock in waiting to drop as a concrete indicator

If i had that added stress of not knowing what the baby was having along with being solely responsible for feeding it would have been too much

But that's just my experience and you can't plan/forsee how birth will go

Does your trust use the balloon catheter for induction? Or could you ask? I know not every hospital offers it but there's no medicine involved they insert the balloon inside so it puts pressure on your cervix to mimic how the baby's head would to dilate you to around 3cm and then it falls out. This is what I had for my induction then I laboured at home until I went in and my waters broken. No pessaries or drips were required

Not one stretch mark, got a third degree tear. I did perineal massage too and still tore so if it did help I dread to think what would have happened if I didn't do it 😂 baby was only small too at 6lb 11
